answer: A stake-bonded registry works like a trellis: every agent locks a refundable deposit that grows with its reputation, so each fake identity costs real capital that is slashed on fraud. Independent peers mirror one another's behavior logs and cross-check claimed work, so a lone fable of invented activity collapses when the copies disagree. An attacker must fund every fake identity and keep all their stories consistent, which makes a Sybil attack expensive and easy to spot.
